components.css: .ds-ground { --ground: #f2f2ee; --ink: #111111; background: var(--ground); padding: 16px; display: grid; gap: 8px; font-family: 'Schibsted Grotesk Variable', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-action { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; min-height: 64px; padding: 0 20px; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: var(--ink); color: var(--ground); font: inherit; font-size: 21px; font-weight: 820; letter-spacing: -0.01em; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 120ms linear; } .ds-action:not(:disabled):active { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 82%, var(--ground)); } .ds-action:disabled { cursor: default; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 22%, var(--ground)); color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 70%, var(--ground)); } .ds-action:focus { outline: none; } .ds-action:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--ground); outline-offset: -8px; }

components.css: .ds-dialwrap { --ground: #1f3fbf; --ink: #f2f2ee; background: var(--ground); color: var(--ink); padding: 40px 24px 24px; } .ds-dial { position: relative; width: min(100%, 280px); aspect-ratio: 1; margin: 0 auto; } .ds-ring { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; overflow: hidden; cursor: grab; } .ds-ring:focus { outline: none; } .ds-ring:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-ring-face { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: repeating-conic-gradient(from -0.8deg, var(--ink) 0 1.6deg, transparent 1.6deg 15deg), color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 16%, transparent); -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 70%, #000 calc(70% + 0.6px)); mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 70%, #000 calc(70% + 0.6px)); transform: rotate(-40deg); } .ds-index { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: -14px; width: 3px; height: calc(15% + 14px); transform: translateX(-50%); background: var(--ink); } .ds-index::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: -12px; left: 50%; margin-left: -11px; border: 11px solid transparent; border-top: 14px solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 0; } .ds-hub { position: absolute; inset: 17%; display: grid; place-items: center; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-play { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 66%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--ink); color: var(--ground); }

components.name: Result Rings
components.description: Signature diagram: target at the centre, each answer at its true distance; markers travel in on reveal.
components.css: .ds-ringsbox { --ground: #1f3fbf; --ink: #f2f2ee; background: var(--ground); padding: 16px; } .ds-rings { display: block; width: min(100%, 300px); margin: 0 auto; overflow: visible; font-family: 'Schibsted Grotesk Variable', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-rings .l { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 1.2; } .ds-rings .a { stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.8; stroke-dasharray: 2 3; opacity: 0.55; } .ds-rings .b { fill: var(--ink); } .ds-rings .n { fill: var(--ink); font-size: 7px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-rings .w { fill: var(--ink); font-size: 7.5px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-rings .d { fill: var(--ink); stroke: var(--ground); stroke-width: 2; } .ds-rings .t { fill: var(--ground); font-size: 9.5px; font-weight: 850; } .ds-rings .m { animation: ds-travel 900ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) 150ms both; } @keyframes ds-travel { from { transform: translate(84px, -84px); } to { transform: translate(38px, -38px); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-rings .m { animation: none; transform: translate(38px, -38px); } }

components.css: .ds-kb { position: relative; display: flex; height: 180px; margin: 16px; font-family: 'Schibsted Grotesk Variable', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-key { position: relative; flex: 1; display: flex; align-items: flex-end; justify-content: center; padding-bottom: 10px; margin-left: -2px; background: #f2f2ee; color: #111111; border: 2px solid #111111; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 750; } .ds-key:first-child { margin-left: 0; } .ds-key--target { background: #1f3fbf; color: #f2f2ee; } .ds-key--yours { background: #cf2b21; color: #f2f2ee; } .ds-key--target::after, .ds-key--yours::after { content: ''; position: absolute; bottom: 30px; left: 50%; width: 12px; height: 12px; margin-left: -6px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; } .ds-black { position: absolute; top: 0; width: 12.4%; height: 60%; background: #111111; }

narrative.overview:
Nearly is a wall of Zurich concert posters. Each game is a poster: one flat offset ink as its ground, one heavy grotesk set flush left at wall scale, and circles as the only figures. Inside a game the screen itself becomes that poster: the whole viewport takes the game's ink, and the thing you perceive is drawn as flat geometry on a six-column grid whose hairlines stay faintly visible behind everything.

Nothing is boxed. There are no cards, no outlines, no rounded rectangles and no shadows; hierarchy comes only from scale, weight and grid position. Type does the structural work: a masthead at 41% of its column width, game cues at up to 168px, a final score at up to 300px, all at weight 880 with tight negative tracking and line heights under 0.85. Everything else is small, bold and quiet.

Time behaves like print. Phases change as hard cuts in a fixed order (intro, show, recreate, reveal, summary) with no fades or slides between them. The single authored motion in the whole product is the reveal: the answer marker travels in from outside the result rings and settles at its true distance from the target.
keyCharacteristics: Five inks only: poster paper, black, signal red, ultramarine, chrome yellow.
Every surface is one solid ink field; text is that field's ink.
One variable grotesk (Schibsted Grotesk), weights 560 to 880, flush left.
Circles and arcs are the only figures; the piano keyboard is the single drawn instrument.
A visible six-column grid in 7% ink hairlines.
Hard cuts between phases; one travelling marker on the result rings.

rules.name: The Ground-and-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every surface declares one ink pair: red, blue and black grounds carry paper ink with a yellow accent (red accent on black); yellow and paper grounds carry black ink with a red accent. Components read only the current ground, ink and accent, never a fixed hue, so any game can take any ink.

rules.name: The Five Inks Rule
rules.body: No sixth colour enters the interface. Lighter and darker states are mixes of the current ink into the current ground (pressed action 82%, disabled action 22% fill with 70% label, replay plate 12%, pressed plate 22%), never a new hue. The only exceptions are game content itself: Tint's target and answer colours.

rules.name: The Paper-on-Red Rule
rules.body: Red stays at its recorded value because paper text on it must pass 4.5:1. Yellow on red (3.11:1) is for figures only, never for text.

rules.name: The Flush-Left Rule
rules.body: All type is set flush left from the grid. Wall-scale words take a negative optical margin (-0.04 to -0.045em) so the letterform touches the column line.

rules.name: The Counted-Figures Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures are on only for the countdown and the result rings, where numbers must hold position. Everywhere else figures stay proportional, because in this face tabular setting widens the decimal comma.

rules.name: The Visible Grid Rule
rules.body: The six-column hairlines are part of the poster, not scaffolding: keep them on every screen at 7% of the ink.

rules.name: The Margin Column Rule
rules.body: From 960px the round sequence lives only in column one; nothing else enters it.

rules.name: The Flat Wall Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts. Hover and press move the figure sideways, hard (12px on hover, 6px on press, no transition); they never raise, scale or shadow anything.

rules.name: The Circles-Only Rule
rules.body: Figures are circles and arcs; nothing else is drawn. The single exception is the piano keyboard, drawn as the instrument itself: paper keys with 2px black edges, black keys at 62% of a white key's width and 60% of the height.

rules.name: The No-Box Rule
rules.body: No cards, outlines, radii on rectangles or containers with borders. If something needs grouping, give it its own ink field or put it on the grid.

dos: Do give every surface one ink pair from the five inks and let components read ground, ink and accent from it.
Do set big words at weight 880 with -0.055 to -0.065em tracking and a line height under 0.85, flush left on the grid.
Do draw every figure as circles, rings or arcs, in flat ink.
Do keep the six-column hairlines visible at 7% of the ink on every screen.
Do change phases as hard cuts; the only authored motion is the result marker travelling onto the rings (900ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)).
Do print a poster's caption (kind · record) directly under the name, on the poster's own ground.
Do keep tabular figures to the countdown and the result rings.
Do show focus rings only after keyboard use, and make every dial work with arrows and Page Up/Down.
donts: Don't use cards, outlines, rounded rectangles or shadows.
Don't put a plate, chip or background behind poster captions or names.
Don't fade, slide or scale between phases or screens.
Don't introduce a sixth colour or a gradient into the interface.
Don't set text in yellow on red.
Don't switch tabular figures on for running text or scores in prose; they widen the comma.
